subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does the gateway security owner agree that socket-local event sequence values are non-secret ordering metadata and that no session-hijacking path exists without defeating authentication, device authorization, or transport security?
rationale: The inspected protocol does not use sequence values as credentials, but a security-labeled report should not be closed until the owner confirms the intended trust boundary or requests private exploit evidence.

options.title: Confirm boundary and close
options.body: Confirm that event sequence predictability is harmless under the authenticated protocol and close unless the reporter supplies a distinct reproducible injection primitive.

options.title: Request private proof
options.body: Keep the issue open while requesting a packet trace or proof of concept showing an unauthenticated or cross-session message accepted by current main.

options.title: Open targeted hardening work
options.body: If the owner identifies a genuine authentication or integrity gap, route it privately and scope remediation to that boundary rather than randomizing ordering counters.

recommendation.title: Confirm boundary and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that event sequence predictability is harmless under the authenticated protocol and close unless the reporter supplies a distinct reproducible injection primitive.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history ties this person most directly to the gateway client and connection protocol surfaces under review.
